name: A warm bubble grows into a cloud (250 m, 20 minutes)
line: A small blob of warm air rises, cools and turns into a growing cloud.
note: Weisman and Klemp's temperature and moisture with almost no wind shear (2 m/s over 6 km). The area is 40 km wide because a run keeps a storm about 18 km from every open side.

changes.why: the time step scaled with the grid spacing
a restart point at the end of the 20 minutes
the damping layer starts 4 km below the 16 km top (CM1's file: 5 km below its 20 km top)
netCDF, which ncview, xarray and most tools read (CM1's file asks for GrADS)
one file per saved time, so each picture has its own file
the sounding is the file input_sounding beside this namelist
the wind comes from the sounding file (CM1 sets iwnd = 0 with isnd = 7)
the moving frame follows the storm this sounding makes (the storm-track check's recommended frame)
the moving frame follows the storm this sounding makes (the storm-track check's recommended frame)

gm1_settings_why: The warm bubble is 4 km across and 2 degrees warmer than its surroundings (CM1's is 20 km across and 1 degree), so it fits the small area. CM1 keeps the bubble in its code, not the namelist, so these are GM1 settings.

sounding.rights: written by GM1 (gpuwm-cm1 preset environment) from Weisman and Klemp's (1982) formulas as CM1 r21.1 base.F transcribes them

environment.method: Weisman and Klemp (1982) temperature and moisture as CM1 r21.1 base.F isnd = 5 builds them, with the boundary-layer mixing-ratio cap set for the CAPE target; wind calm at the ground with the chosen 0-6 km shear (curved: CM1's iwnd = 2 shape, scaled)
